title: Software Architect
tagline: Shape how large systems and teams fit together, and make the big trade-offs.
about: Software architects make the decisions that are expensive to change: system boundaries, data ownership, technology choices and how teams' work fits together. They write, draw and explain as much as they code.
It's a senior role you grow into after several years of building software. This path organises what to study along the way.
day: Write design documents and decision records
Balance cost, reliability, speed and simplicity

nodes.d: Several years shipping, operating and maintaining software is the foundation.
Modularity, coupling, cohesion and managing complexity.

phases.title: Architecture fundamentals
phases.goal: The concepts and vocabulary of architecture.

nodes.d: Monoliths, modular monoliths, microservices, event-driven and serverless.
Performance, scalability, availability, security and their trade-offs.
Model the business and draw boundaries around it.
Diagrams and decision records others can understand.
links: The C4 model for software architecture

nodes.d: Consistency, replication, failure and the CAP trade-offs.

project.d: Write a design document with C4 diagrams and three ADRs for a real or realistic system, including alternatives considered and why they were rejected.

nodes.d: Design large systems end to end.
Change architecture incrementally as needs change.
Security designed in, not bolted on.
Explain trade-offs to engineers and executives alike.
links: The Architecture of Open Source Applications

nodes.d: Study how successful open-source systems are designed.
links: The Architecture of Open Source Applications

interview: Large-scale system design with trade-off discussion.
Present a past architecture decision and its outcome.
Review a flawed design and propose improvements.
Behavioural: leading technical change across teams.
